q: How do I package a project from a script?
a: Run `projects.package` with `path` (the project file) and `destination` (the folder to put it in). Add `"proxies": true` to include proxies, `"format": "file"` for a single `.revpkg` file instead of a folder, or `"dryRun": true` to write nothing and just get `estimateBytes`.

q: What is the manifest.json inside a package?
a: A list of every file in the package: its path inside the package, its size and its SHA-256 checksum, plus what was left out on purpose (the render cache, which is rebuilt; downloaded AI models; proxies unless chosen). Revolution writes it after reading every copied file once more. It holds only paths inside the package, nothing about your own disk. On import Revolution checks every file against it.

q: How do I open a package someone sent me?
a: On the Project Manager home screen click Import Package (`projects.importPackage`) and choose the `.revpkg` file, or for a package folder the `manifest.json` inside it. The project goes into the folder of the projects list you are looking at. Revolution checks every file first, then copies the package into your projects folder and points every clip at its copy, so nothing is offline.

q: Can I cancel a package that's taking ages?
a: Yes. Packaging runs in the background with progress in the status bar and can be stopped. When you stop it, the half-made package folder is removed, and an existing package folder is never overwritten.

q: Where exactly does the package end up?
a: In the folder you pick, as `<destination>/<project name> package/` holding the project file, every media file it uses and `manifest.json` (and the used custom shader effects in `Effects/`). With the one-file option it is a single `<project name>.revpkg` there instead.

q: Is camera footage recompressed when I make an .revpkg?
a: No. An `.revpkg` is a zip with every file stored as it is, so camera media isn't recompressed and nothing is re-encoded. The folder it is made from is removed afterwards.

q: What doesn't go into a package?
a: The render cache (it is rebuilt), downloaded AI models, and proxies unless you choose them (`"proxies": true`); `manifest.json` lists these as left out on purpose. Custom shader effects the project doesn't use stay home.

q: A package has a shader effect with the same file name as one of mine. Which one is kept?
a: Yours. On import, custom shader effects from the package's `Effects/` folder are added to your own Effects folder, but one you already have under the same file name is never replaced.

q: Does importing a package check the files before copying them?
a: Yes. Revolution first checks every file against the manifest: is it there, the right size, the same checksum. That reads the whole package once, in the background. If anything is missing or damaged, the import stops, names the files and copies nothing.

q: Can projects.import open a package folder?
a: Yes: `projects.import` of a folder that has a Revolution `manifest.json` does the same as `projects.importPackage`, checking every file and relinking the clips to their copies.

q: Does a package carry my scratch disk settings to the other computer?
a: No. The packaged project uses the receiver's own scratch disks, not yours (your folders would mean nothing on their computer). The Color page's saved comparison frames travel in a folder next to the project and are found on the receiver's scratch disks after import.

q: And how does the person on the other end know nothing got corrupted?
a: The package's `manifest.json` has every file's size and SHA-256 checksum. When they click Import Package (`projects.importPackage`), Revolution checks every file against it before copying anything; a missing or damaged file stops the import with its name, e.g. the package is incomplete (damaged: clip.mov).
prev: How do I hand a finished project to a colourist on a USB disk?

q: can it be just one file? emailing a folder is a pain
a: Yes: in the project tile's menu choose Package as One File… (`projects.menu.package-file`), or run `projects.package` with `"format": "file"`. You get a single `<project name>.revpkg` (a zip that stores every file as it is, so nothing is recompressed). Import Package takes the `.revpkg` directly.

context.q: i need to give my project to my editor friend
context.a: Use Package on the Project Manager home screen: it copies the project, all its media and a manifest with checksums into one package folder they can import with Import Package.
